name: Western Desert (Egypt)
headline: Sand, swing, and open sightlines
story: Egypt's Western Desert pairs dune seas with gravel plains and almost no vegetation. The result is a clean, open test surface with a strong day-night air swing for thermal rehearsals.
transfers: Almost no vegetation (MODIS NDVI 0.090) — wheels meet soil and rock rather than root mat
31 K day–night air swing (NASA POWER) for thermal-cycling practice
Slope still unknown — it will use the same 20 m baseline as Jezero and the lunar poles
breaks: Earth's gravity and thick atmosphere do not transfer
Light and radiation are planetary, not terrestrial
Mineralogy is blank until a citable site value exists
Air temperature here is not the same as ground temperature
tests: Run a full thermal soak through a site day–night cycle
Drive a wheel–soil test once 20 m slopes are filled
Rehearse a timed rover shift under thermal stress
scaleNotes: Screen cell ~0.5°. Vegetation: MODIS 250 m point sample. Slopes: pending shared 20 m baseline. Temperature: air, NASA POWER.

gaps.title: Gravity mismatch
gaps.detail: Earth 1 g vs Moon ~1/6 g / Mars ~0.38 g — loads and sinkage do not scale 1:1.

gaps.title: Atmosphere / vacuum
gaps.detail: Convective cooling and pressure effects on Earth invalidate vacuum thermal behavior.

gaps.title: Radiation environment
gaps.detail: Earth magnetosphere and atmosphere shield radiation; planetary surface dose does not transfer.

gaps.title: Air vs ground temperature
gaps.detail: Jezero MEDA diurnal amplitude used here is air (~60 K at 1.45 m). Earth POWER uses T2M air — compare air↔air. MODIS LST is ground and must not be mixed unlabeled.

gaps.title: Vegetation sample scale
gaps.detail: NDVI is a MODIS 250 m point sample in a ~2 km box at the cell centre, not a 0.5° area mean. Bare cover within the cell can differ from the sample.

gaps.title: Biosphere / contamination
gaps.detail: Earth biology and planetary protection constraints are unique to terrestrial tests.

name: Taklamakan
headline: A cold desert stress test
story: The Taklamakan sits in a mountain-ringed basin, with migrating dunes and dust that punish seals, bearings and optics. Its aridity and temperature swing make it a useful worst-case site.
